To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an ultrasensitive surface plasmon-based approach that allows for simultaneous detection and analysis of conformational changes of multiple proteins operating in a complex signaling network, such as the phototransduction pathway in the retina.

a planar plasmomic device allows for simultaneous detection, over a broad range of Ca2+ concentrations, of the conformation dynamics of multiple Ca2+-sensor proteins, which operate in the vertebrate visual phototransduction process.

the surface plasmon-based biosensor allows the simultaneous monitoring of conformational transitions in four Ca(2+) binding proteins in a single assay, and the analysis of the effects of cations on the conformational transitions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of a new class of biosensing devices, which are capable of detecting the dynamics of conformational switches of Ca(2+ )sensor proteins, which operate in the vertebrate visual phototransduction process.
the development of novel biosensing technologies based on surface plasmon resonances (SPR).
the development of novel nanoscale devices to study the dynamics of biological systems.

The main takeaway from our work is that
SPR is a valuable tool for the quantitative study of the dynamics of Ca(2+)/Mg(2+)-sensing proteins in the context of complex signaling networks.
the conformational dynamics detected by SPR can be exploited to study the Ca(2+)/Mg(2+)-dependent conformational changes in a variety of Ca(2+)+-binding proteins.
the SPR-based approach allows the detection of conformation changes of Ca(2+):sensor proteins in a quantitative and comparative manner.
